clue.text: Society has high opinion of Greek philosopher

parts.note: to rate someone is to think highly of them, so 'has high opinion of' gives rates

explanation.surface: A club's members hold an ancient thinker in great esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Society has' reads like a subject and verb, but the verb phrase is a piece in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Athenian thinker who taught Plato and questioned everyone in the marketplace.

clue.text: Look, new lace design

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of the next two words are made into something new

explanation.surface: Admiring a freshly made lace pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' sits between definition and fodder, and only 'lace design' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideways peek out of the corner of the eye is a brief kind of look.

clue.text: Doctor continued to nurse sovereign

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one piece cradles the other

parts.note: a sultan is a Muslim sovereign

explanation.surface: A physician keeps on caring for a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' suits a doctor's surface, but here it means hold one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior hospital doctor in Britain holds the rank of specialist in charge of patients.

clue.text: Representative to get old religious books

parts.note: to age is to get old
NT is the New Testament, a set of religious books

explanation.surface: A delegate is sent to fetch some ancient scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old religious books' looks like OT, but 'old' goes with 'to get'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acts on another's behalf is their agent or representative.

clue.text: A nurse stayed out for 24 hours in spring

indicators.note: out means wrong or not in place, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nurse stayed away for a whole day sometime in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of the story of an absent nurse, but it is the signal to rearrange A NURSE STAYED.
explanation.definitionFit: The day of the Christian festival of the Resurrection falls in spring, a single day.

clue.text: Sand blowing about in outskirts of Greek port

indicators.note: in tells us the scrambled letters go inside the outer pair
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters, here those of Greek
sand blowing about is scattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sand drifts around the edges of a harbour town in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek port' looks like the definition, but 'Greek' only supplies its outer letters; the port is in Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a major Baltic seaport in northern Poland, once called Danzig.

clue.text: Bill wearing close-fitting jacket for a performance

indicators.note: wearing a jacket is being inside it

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket of the Renaissance
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: An actor called Bill dons a tight-fitting period jacket for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name, but it gives AC, for account.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy partnership's routine, two people working together on stage, is a kind of performance.

clue.text: Steal, and you could end up here

explanation.surface: Thieve, and this is where you might land.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: to steal, and a prison or police station.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word both for stealing and for a jail where thieves are locked up.

clue.text: Was acquainted with audio version of novel

indicators.note: an audio version is something heard, so we want a word sounding like the synonym

parts.note: novel means new

explanation.surface: Someone knew the audiobook edition of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book, but it is the adjective meaning fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: To have been familiar with someone or something is the past sense of know.

clue.text: Sue's bowled over embraced by European performer

indicators.note: being embraced by someone is being held inside their arms, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a Dane, from Denmark, is a European

indicators.note: something bowled over is knocked flat and turned head over heels, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the name with its 's read as an S

explanation.surface: Sue is knocked off her feet and then hugged by a visitor from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' suggests Sue was delighted, but it signals a reversal; 'performer' here is a ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: A danseuse is a female ballet dancer, someone who performs on stage.

clue.text: He goes after large portion of fast food

indicators.note: goes after places one piece behind the other in the answer
a large portion of a word is most of it, here all but its last letter

parts.note: fast means quick

explanation.surface: A man hurries off after a big helping of a takeaway meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast food' looks like one phrase, but 'fast' belongs to the wordplay and 'food' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiche is a savoury open tart with an egg filling, a dish people eat.

clue.text: An upset over Chinese rulers invading Somalia's capital

annotationWithheld.why: An upset over Chinese rulers invading Somalia's capital (5,7): wordplay is S (first of Somalia's) + AN + TODO + O with MING inside, so 'capital' must be both the first-letter indicator and the definition
annotationWithheld.clue: An upset over Chinese rulers invading Somalia's capital

clue.text: Be mad to climb barrier in Berlin, once

parts.note: to climb is to go up
the Berlin Wall divided the city from 1961 to 1989 and was known simply as the Wall

explanation.surface: Escaping East Germany meant scaling the famous dividing wall, which seemed crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for becoming furious or frantic describes being mad with anger.

clue.text: Boisterous reprobate giving loud cry

parts.note: a rip is an old word for a rake or reprobate
roaring means giving a loud cry

explanation.surface: A rowdy scoundrel bellowing loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy, wild and full of energy describes something boisterous.

clue.text: The Sound of Music premiered in Liverpool beery mates ruined

definitions.text: The Sound of Music premiered in Liverpool

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Drunken friends in Liverpool spoil a performance of the famous musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Sound of Music' looks like the film musical, but here it is a style of music.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1960s pop style from Liverpool, led by the Beatles, was a sound born on Merseyside.

clue.text: Might they come into recital to sing?

definitions.text: Might they come into recital to sing?

indicators.note: the voices come into the clue's words, sitting inside them as a run of letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether certain singers will join a concert performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'recital to sing'. The whole clue also describes choir voices joining a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: These are lower female or boy voices who might well join a concert to sing.

clue.text: German prince is turning up, say, exhausted in America

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
EG, for example, is signalled by say
fried is American slang for worn out

explanation.surface: A German royal arrives and, apparently, is worn out in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses IS to give SI.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the hero of Germanic legend and Wagner's opera, a royal son.

clue.text: Games of tennis for each team's reserves

parts.note: a tennis match is played in sets
a, as in 'a pound a head', means for each
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A list of tennis matches and the substitutes sitting on each team's bench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserves' looks like a noun for substitutes, but it is the verb, to keep something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for later is to put it to one side for future use.

clue.text: Business editor is worried

parts.note: a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: The business editor is anxious about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being troubled or anxious about something is a synonym of being worried.

clue.text: Fish about for some protective covers

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sprat is a small fish

explanation.surface: Anglers fish around for some waterproof sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarpaulin sheets, shortened, are waterproof covers thrown over goods or boats.

clue.text: Fight involving FBI agents and sailor is broken up

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: a fray is a fight or brawl
G-men, short for government men, is old slang for FBI agents
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A brawl between federal agents and a seaman is broken up by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in pieces or incomplete is fragmentary, made of broken bits.

clue.text: Old city not to be found in uncultivated province formerly

indicators.note: something not found in a word is removed from it

parts.note: natural means wild or uncultivated
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: An ancient town cannot be located in a wild region of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove UR from NATURAL to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a South African province, renamed KwaZulu-Natal in 1994.

clue.text: Errant husband covers up in this way

indicators.note: the clue words cover the run of letters, holding it out of sight inside them

explanation.surface: An unfaithful husband hides his tracks in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb for 'so' or 'in this manner' is a formal synonym of in this way.

clue.text: She supplies wonderful food but no starter

indicators.note: no starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: manna is the miraculous food from heaven in the Bible

explanation.surface: A woman who serves splendid meals, but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' sounds like a first course, but it is the first letter, the M of MANNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's name, so it can be any she.

clue.text: Don't give up executin' offenders

explanation.surface: A plea to persevere, and a dropped-g reference to sending criminals to the gallows.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped g in 'executin'' tells you to drop the g of the second sense too.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to hold on through trouble; hanging is how criminals were once executed.

clue.text: Number about to hit out

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A boxer counts down, about to throw a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'ready to', but 'about' reverses NO and 'to hit' gives STRIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who have walked out in an industrial dispute are said to be out.

clue.text: Opening of store that's convenient for drink

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here that of store

parts.note: handy means convenient

explanation.surface: A local shop that is handy when you want something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a common British pub drink.

clue.text: Enough to keep things simmering in a dull event

explanation.surface: A gentle heat on the stove, and an occasion that falls flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the answer as two words: the small flame that keeps a pan simmering.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle flame keeps a pot just bubbling; a disappointing moment is the opposite of a highlight.
